$comment: Accepted exceptions for scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs (#4632).
SHRINK-ONLY and hand-edited under review: the checker fails on a stale entry, so a
site that gets fixed must have its entry deleted in the same PR. There is deliberately
no `--fix`/`--update` flag — a generator would let a new violation be admitted by
'just run the update command', which is precisely how a gate stops meaning anything.
Every entry names WHY it is still here and WHAT closes it.
Key granularity is `<file>::<callee>`, NOT a line — line numbers churn on every
unrelated edit and a line-keyed ledger would go stale constantly. The cost is that an
entry licenses the WHOLE file for that callee: a genuinely new silent swallow of the
same callee in an already-listed file would be excused. Read the entry's `sites` list
as the set it was reviewed against, and re-review when that file grows a new one.
CURRENTLY EMPTY — the intended steady state, not a dormant file. The two entries #4754
added were never debt: they described CORRECT code (a `/meta` PUT that answers the
caller a 4xx/422 error envelope, and two batch operations that write each failure into
the per-item outcome report that IS their contract). The gate simply had no way to say
'the failure was handed to the caller', so correct code had to be parked in a ledger
whose header calls every line debt — and the cheapest way out was to bolt a durability
`error` onto a path whose common case is a rejected request, which is exactly the
mirror-image failure AGENTS.md warns about. #5241 fixed the GATE instead: it now carries
a declared failure-propagation vocabulary (FAILURE_PROPAGATION_CALLEES, plus the
function-scoped FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES) and proves structurally that every path out
of the catch delivers the failure. Both entries went stale and were deleted.
So: an entry here means a REAL degradation that is not yet fixed. If a red seam turns
out to hand its failure to the caller instead, it does not belong in this file — declare
HOW it delivers, in the checker's vocabulary, and let the checker verify the shape.
